title: Enterprise capacity triage workflow for SLA negotiation and heterogeneous GPU mapping
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Enterprise customers requesting dedicated capacity frequently provide incomplete signals (QPS spikes, model variants, acceptable latency bands) and often require heterogeneous GPU families for cost/throughput tradeoffs. We lack a repeatable intake + decision workflow that: 1) captures minimal viable signals for SLA negotiation; 2) scores requests consistently against capacity and risk; 3) outputs a recommended GPU-class mapping and scaling policy with clear fallbacks. Goal: Define a triage workflow and artifacts (interview script, scoring rubric, decision matrix, preflight test checklist) that enable PM/Capacity Concierge to respond within 3 business days with a recommended capacity profile and escalation path.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Intake form + interview script created and approved by PM and Capacity Engineering
A2: Scoring rubric documented with numeric thresholds for Low/Medium/High capacity risk
A3: Decision matrix that maps workload signatures to GPU class recommendations (A100, H100, L4, mixed pools)
A4: Preflight test checklist and automated smoke test template present in GitHub (links added)
A5: Playbook for SLA negotiation including default fallback policies accepted by Sales and SRE
triage_rubric: Workload footprint (0-10): tokens/sec * avg_seq_length normalized; >8 => high throughput
Latency tolerance (0-10): inverse of p95 latency requirement; tight SLAs score higher
Burst ratio (0-10): peak/steady; >10 => needs burst-capable pool or burst credits
Model complexity (0-10): parameter count & kv-cache pressure; large context models score higher
Data sensitivity (0-10): regulatory/PII requires private/VPC; flags for KMS/HSM
Total score interpretation: 0-20 Low; 21-35 Medium; 36-50 High. Map to recommended lane: shared-dedicated hybrid / reserved single-family / multi-family pool with affinity
interview_script: 1) Primary use case and SLA objective (p95 target, p99 target, acceptable tail behavior)
2) Expected steady QPS and peak QPS, and expected duration of peaks
3) Typical sequence length distribution and example prompts (attach sample traces)
4) Models and versions planned for production; willingness to accept quantized variants
6) Tolerance for fallbacks: slower model, degraded quality, or queueing during capacity pressure
7) Billing and commitment expectations (commit hours/monthly; burst budget)
decision_matrix_examples: Scenario A: Medium steady QPS (200 reqs/s), p95 200ms, small seqs, model Llama2-Chat-7B => Recommendation: reserved L4 family with autoscale floor + 20% burst credit; provide rollout canary at 10% traffic

Scenario B: High bursty workload (steady 10 reqs/s, burst to 10k for up to 30 minutes), p95 500ms => Recommendation: hybrid reserved pool + burstable shared capacity; set burst policy with preemption rules and SLA caveat; require preflight stress test

Scenario C: Regulated PII workload, medium throughput, strict p99 300ms => Recommendation: private/VPC deployment on dedicated H100/A100 depending on model; require KMS integration and audit logging; SLA offered after staging validation
